name: Dyna-Westdrive
description: Understanding active affective engagement requires multimodal data collected in ecologically valid, interactive contexts. This combination is rarely achieved in existing affective datasets. We introduce Dyna-Westdrive, a large-scale, VR-native multimodal dataset designed for behavior and emotion analysis through embedded wearable sensing. The dataset comprises recordings from 300 participants immersed in a high-fidelity driving simulation using an instrumented headmounted display equipped with heart-rate monitoring, eyetracking, lower-face video, and audio capture, synchronized with steering dynamics and virtual event triggers. Eight eventdriven stress-inducing scenarios elicit naturalistic affective responses under controlled, ethically acceptable conditions. We detail the full pipeline: VR scenario design, multimodal data acquisition, heterogeneous signal preprocessing, and a multi-rater continuous valence-arousal annotation framework. By combining active participant-driven interaction and noninvasive multimodal sensing, Dyna-Westdrive enables research on cross-modal affective dynamics in a domain with direct relevance to driver state monitoring and human-vehicle interaction.
